subject: Feature gating + staggered rollout for Bank Horizon pilot
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Feature gating + staggered rollout for Bank Horizon pilot

Hi Karthik/Markus —

Quick summary: Bank Horizon (prospect) verbally committed to a 6-week pilot if we can guarantee a staggered rollout model and per-route gating for production traffic during the pilot. Their procurement team (cc'd separately in the thread with Sally) needs comfort that we can: 1) partially enable the new inference route for a subset of tenants/users, 2) throttle/failover to a fallback model on capacity pressure, and 3) provide traceable per-request logs for the pilot window.

Customer priority/timeline: they want pilot start week of Dec 7 and a go/no-go decision by Nov 10. They are willing to sign an MOU and pay for a reserved capacity trial.

Asks for product/eng: can we slot a P1 for a limited-scope sprint to implement the gating primitives + a temporary routing policy that supports:
- per-route enable flag (tenant-scoped)
- soft-traffic percentage (0-100% gradual ramp)
- fallback to a lower-capacity variant if latency SLOs breach
- basic audit logs tied to request-id (not full export, but retained for 30 days)

Attachments: BH-SoW-v2.pdf (customer draft), Horizon-security-questions.xlsx (their initial compliance questionnaire), pilot-rollout-draft.odt (sales suggested plan).

I know we have existing work on rollout/rollbacks but this would be a focused, short-lived capability specifically requested by a revenue-significant deal. Please advise feasibility, approx engineering effort, and any blocking design questions.

Thanks —
Camila
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feature gating + staggered rollout for Bank Horizon pilot

Thanks Camila — good write-up. A few quick clarifying questions so we can scope correctly:

1) When you say "per-route enable flag (tenant-scoped)", do they expect this to be controllable via the Redwood Console UI, or is a single-off config change per tenant (engineer flip) acceptable for the pilot?
2) The "soft-traffic percentage" — is this expected to be applied at the gateway (edge) level or in the serving runtime (we have different knobs and trade-offs)?
3) For the "fallback to lower-capacity variant": do they mean a quantized model variant we already host, or simply route to a different model family (e.g., smaller model)?
4) Logging: confirm they only need request-id, timestamp, route name, and status/latency. No PII payload logging?

High level feasibility: engineering-wise this is doable as a scoped effort if we constrain scope to console toggle + API flag + simple percentage-based sampling at the router level with an automated failover condition (latency threshold + error rate). Full, audited export will push scope. I'll work with Markus to get a rough T-shirt estimate.

If this is customer-critical revenue, we should capture it as a short-term feature commit and schedule a canary plan.

- Karthik
Product Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feature gating + staggered rollout for Bank Horizon pilot

Quick note from infra/serving standpoint:
- Router-level percentage sampling is straightforward (0.5–1 sprint to wire into current router), but full tenant isolation (KV cache separation) will add complexity depending on whether they require cold-start eviction guarantees.
- For failover/fallback we need a clear SLO threshold (p50/p95 latency + error rate). Who will own the threshold config? Console vs. ops-runbook?
- For the logs: storing request-id + route + latency for 30 days is fine. If procurement asks for delivery of those logs as a feed, that is additional work (export pipeline).

I can pencil in a spike to validate router changes Monday; need Karthik to confirm exact scope for the pilot so we can estimate.

— Markus
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feature gating + staggered rollout for Bank Horizon pilot

Answers inline:
1) Console toggle preferred but customer accepts API/one-time engineer flip for the pilot (they just need ability to ramp quickly).
2) Gateway-level percentage sampling is preferred by the customer because it integrates with their traffic shaping. They said edge sampling is fine as long as routing is traceable back to the tenant.
3) Fallback: they prefer a smaller model variant in our catalog (we already discussed quantized variant with them). If we can offer an automatic route to a pre-registered fallback model, they will be satisfied.
4) Logging: they explicitly said NO request payloads. They want request-id, route name, latency, status, and a tie-back to tenant-id. 30 days retention is OK.

Additional notes: procurement is asking for a one-page description of the pilot controls for their security team. I'm attaching the security questionnaire they sent. They are open to signing the MOU contingent on an internal engineering sign-off that the pilot controls exist.

Bottom line ask to Product/Eng: can we commit to delivering the scoped primitives as described above (console toggle optional) as a prioritized work item before Nov 10 so we can give the customer a go/no-go? If not, please indicate what minimum subset we can guarantee by that date.

Camila

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feature gating + staggered rollout for Bank Horizon pilot

Proposed minimal rollout plan (for Nov 10 go/no-go):
- Week 1 (Nov 3–9): Spike + prototype router-level percentage sampling and register a fallback model (1 engineer, 1 infra)
- Week 2 (Nov 10–16): Integration tests, create pilot runbook, and prepare the one-page controls doc for procurement
- Week 3 (Nov 17–23): Customer-facing dry run with traces; if dry run passes, schedule Dec 7 pilot start

I recommend we treat this as P1 for the week of Nov 3 so we can meet the Nov 10 decision deadline. If Product/Eng can only do a partial commit (e.g., router sampling + logs but not console toggle), we should communicate that as the minimum acceptable for the MOU.

Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feature gating + staggered rollout for Bank Horizon pilot

Thanks all — this is excellent and actionable.

ASK: Can Product/Eng confirm by end of day Nov 5 whether they can accept P1 slot for the Week of Nov 3 spike and agree on the minimum deliverable for Nov 10? If we cannot commit, I will escalate to GTM leadership because procurement will push their alternative vendors.

Customer note (from last call): they are willing to cover some engineering time as an uplift if necessary — we should capture that in the MOU language.

Camila

-- End of thread --
